_note: Preparation guidance for a 62443-3-2 zones-and-conduits risk assessment: the documents a consultant most commonly needs, the ones clients often forget, and the stakeholders worth interviewing. ADVISORY ONLY, not a fixed checklist, and it must never pre-populate the basis-of-assessment register; the consultant records what was actually reviewed/observed there.
commonDocuments: Network architecture diagrams of the network as it is now
Asset inventory for the systems in scope
P&IDs and process descriptions for the processes the SUC controls
PHA or HAZOP results, the usual source for the worst credible impact
Any existing segmentation or zone and conduit documentation
The client's corporate risk matrix and tolerable risk criteria
The remote access register, with routes, vendors and standing tunnels
Interface and data flow lists between OT, the DMZ and corporate IT
oftenForgotten: The safety requirements specification for the SIS, which drives the safety zone decisions
Vendor contracts that promise remote access
A wireless site survey or a list of the wireless links into the site
How engineering laptops, USB drives and other portable devices are used, since 3-2 expects them in a zone of their own
Regulatory or insurance constraints that set risk criteria
Previous cyber risk assessments and what happened to their actions
Who in the asset owner's organisation decides the tolerable risk
keyStakeholders: Asset owner senior management, who decide the tolerable risk and sign off the SL-T
Process safety engineer, for consequence severity and the SIS
Control systems engineer, for how the system works in practice
OT or plant network engineer, and their corporate network counterpart
Operations manager, for the essential functions and the worst-case outcomes
System integrator or main vendor representative
IT security or SOC lead, for the threat context and the monitoring in place
